reason: Escape closes the Settings menu together with its Time zone submenu and returns focus to the Settings button that opened them; the screenshot shows that button focused with its ring. Focus lands on the control the user just used, not on the page body.
criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order: after the whole menu closes, focus returns to the Settings button that opened it, a logical place that keeps the user's position. Returning to the Time zone item matters only when the submenu closes alone; here the whole menu closes. 2.4.7 Focus Visible: the Settings button shows a ring in the screenshot. 2.1.2: Escape works and focus is not trapped.

reason: The category name field in the Create category dialog has no label, aria-label, title or placeholder, and Chrome exposes it as textbox with an empty name. The dialog has no name either (reach shows an empty dialog name), so a screen-reader user lands in a blank field with no cue what to type. Guidance puts an unnamed form control at high.

The sentence under Create category is an h3 (level 3, with a link in it) but is drawn as body text, so heading navigation lists it as a section heading. That is a minor 1.3.1 mismatch between markup and presentation.

reason: The flagged span is a focus-trap guard: tabindex 0, aria-hidden, 1px and clipped, inside the open Keyword popover. Tab and Shift+Tab through the popover never leave focus on a guard; every press lands on a real control (search field, Filter button, Amount, the Keyword trigger). The accessibility tree ignores the guard.
criterionAnalysis: 4.1.2: the guard is ignored by the accessibility tree and never holds focus, so no component is exposed without a name or role. 2.4.3 and 2.4.7: Tab and Shift+Tab never rest on a guard, so focus order and focus visibility are unaffected. 1.3.1: the guard conveys nothing. axe flags aria-hidden plus tabindex 0, but no user meets the hidden-but-focusable element the rule warns about.
